meta.title: Yukikaki — AI-native hackathons for Sapporo and beyond
meta.description: AI-native hackathons that accelerate ideas into reality, for Sapporo and beyond. Like Peatix or Luma — but for hackathons, with the prep done and the funding found. Find and join local hackathons, design charrettes and test-kitchen sessions. Project Yukikaki handles the nemawashi and mise en place (problems, data, buy-in, venue, teams) and automatically matches grants and subsidies to every project.

nav.tagline: AI-native hackathons for Sapporo and beyond.

party.title: Bring any team. Our helpers fill in the rest.
party.lead: Any team can show up: a few students, a town office, a shop owner and a friend, or a weekend hackathon squad. We're building AI helpers, friendly helper robots, that will cover the prep roles nobody on your team has yet. It isn't live yet; join the waitlist and we'll tell you when it is.

party.demoHint: Pick everyone you've got. This preview uses a fixed mapping in your browser; it's not the live product.

party.guardrails: Same rules as the rest of Yukikaki: helpers propose and people decide, they cite sources or say they can't, and private data stays private.

kitchen.title: A test kitchen for your town
kitchen.lead: In a test kitchen, chefs try a new dish, taste it, adjust and try again before anything goes on the menu. Yukikaki does the same for local problems: small batches, local ingredients (local data, local partners), low cost and low risk.

step1.title: Bring a problem
step1.body: A resident or shop owner talks through the headache in a short voice interview. It comes back as a clear, scoped brief.

step2.title: Prototype in days
step2.body: Students and builders cook up a fix in days, not months, working with stand-in data so nothing private leaves the shop.

step3.title: Taste it in real work
step3.body: The owner tries the fix during a normal week. The team lead stays on for 90 days to adjust the recipe.

step4.title: Keep, rework or drop
step4.body: An impact check counts the hours saved. What works stays on the menu; the rest is reworked or dropped, with no hard feelings.

kitchen.loop: Then on to the next problem. Each round adds a dish to the town's menu.
kitchen.closing: Every town deserves a test kitchen.

formats.title: One harness, any format
formats.lead: Yukikaki is the rig that holds an event together. The same prep, the same guardrails (the host approves every output, sources are cited or we say we can't, private data stays private, one named owner) and the same follow-through, whatever the format.

kitchenQuest.title: A test kitchen for your town
kitchenQuest.lead: Follow one problem around the kitchen: idea → prototype in days → in real use. Small batches, local ingredients, low cost and low risk, and nothing goes on the menu until the owner has tasted it.

steps.title: Bring a problem
steps.body: A shop owner drops a headache in the box: “Our winter orders still come in by fax, and I retype every one.”
steps.does: A short voice interview becomes a bilingual brief, grounded in official sources.

steps.title: Prototype in days
steps.body: A student team cooks up a fix in days, not months. One named lead owns it from first sketch to hand-over.
steps.does: The team builds with synthetic stand-in data, so nothing private leaves the shop.

steps.title: Taste it in real work
steps.body: The fix is delivered, and the owner tries it during a normal week, at the real counter, with real customers.
steps.does: After delivery, the team lead supports the owner for 90 days to adjust the recipe.

steps.title: Keep, rework or drop
steps.body: Did it earn a place on the menu? Keep it, rework it, or drop it with no hard feelings.
steps.does: An impact check (hours saved each week, owner satisfaction) makes the call.

kitchenQuest.sceneAlt: 8-bit pixel art of a wooden hall on a snowy night with four stations along a snowy floor: a mailbox with a speech bubble, two builders at a desk with a glowing prototype, a shopkeeper tasting at a counter, and a chalkboard showing a check, a wrench and a cross.
kitchenQuest.loop: Then on to the next problem. Each round adds a dish to the town's menu.

landing.p1: AI drafts briefs, matches and checks. A named person approves every one.
landing.p2: Every claim links to its source. When there is no source, it says so.
landing.p3: Every challenge has an owner, and every team has a lead the owner can reach.
landing.p4: Private data stays private. When real data can't be shared, clearly labelled synthetic stand-ins take its place.
landing.p5: Challenges come from businesses in the town, in their own words.
landing.p6: Fewer hands, same town. Owners, builders and the town share the work.
landing.w1: Fewer hands, same town. One screen to approve everything, and a running tally of hours given back.
landing.w2: The task that eats your week, handled, plus a lead who answers your questions for 90 days.
landing.w3: A real problem, real data and a real owner from the first hour. Work that ships and gets used.
landing.w4: Support that lands in the community, with measured impact you can point to.
landing.testimonialsNote: Quotes appear exactly as owners gave them in their impact review.
landing.closingBody: Bring a problem from your business, or bring Yukikaki to your town.
landing.footerStory: Your test kitchen for ideas and prototypes. Like snow shoveling, we clear the path so builders can get to work.
